tool_schemas.description: Release history for a service with health status (oldest first).

tool_schemas.name: rollback

args.summary: After deploying v2.3.1, checkout-api failed health checks in all production regions with an 18% error rate. Rolled back all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) to the most recent healthy release, v2.3.0. First rollback attempt failed after us-east due to an orchestrator error, leaving mixed versions; a retry completed the rollout. Service is now healthy on v2.3.0 in all regions with error rate reduced to 0.2%. v2.3.1 should be investigated before redeploying.
args.title: checkout-api unhealthy after v2.3.1 deploy — rolled back to v2.3.0

trace.error_message: Request to create_incident timed out after 30000ms

trace.final:
All done. Here's a summary:

**Actions taken:**
1. **Diagnosed the issue**: checkout-api on v2.3.1 (latest deploy) was failing health checks with an 18% error rate across all regions. The most recent release that was healthy in production was **v2.3.0**.
2. **Rolled back to v2.3.0**: The first rollback attempt hit a partial failure (orchestrator error), leaving us-east on v2.3.0 but us-west and eu-west still on broken v2.3.1. I retried the rollback, which completed successfully across all regions.
3. **Verified recovery**: checkout-api is now healthy on v2.3.0 in us-east, us-west, and eu-west, with error rate down from 18% to 0.2%.
4. **Opened SEV2 incident** (INC-0001) documenting the v2.3.1 failure, the rollback (including the initial partial failure and retry), and a note that v2.3.1 should be investigated before any redeploy. The incident creation call initially timed out, but I confirmed via list_incidents that it was actually created — no duplicate needed.

**Recommendation**: Investigate the v2.3.1 changes and re-test before redeploying; v2.3.1 has never been healthy in production.
